title: Edge-log CLV equals the edge on every settled row: 'closing' snapshots are copies of the opening prices, stamped after tip-off
steps: Open /results, section 'Every edge we've shown': Avg CLV +3.8%, '100% beat the close'.

In edges_log, all 6 settled rows have closing_price == price_taken and clv == edge_pct (e.g. Hawks +3.5: 2.04 / 2.04, clv 0.037879 = edge 0.037879; Jazz ML 7 / 7, 0.029473; St Mary's 1.51 / 1.51, 0.073478).

odds_snapshots for nba-fa3e335565eb02c2: the 'closing' pull (pulled_at 01:00:22) has the same prices AND the same book timestamps (ts 03:07–03:08) as the 'pregame' pull at 00:08:22; tip-off was 01:11:22. A book timestamp 2 hours after the pull time and after the game started cannot be real.
expected: Closing lines come from a later snapshot than the opening one, with book timestamps at or before the pull time, so CLV measures something.
actual: CLV is identical to the opening edge by construction, so the headline 'Avg CLV +3.8%, 100% beat the close' (and picks avgClv 0.0400996) carries no information. The formula itself is right: I recomputed p_close × price_taken − 1 for all 6 rows and 5 pick_results and every value matches to 1e-6.
evidence: Numbers above; /results text captured in scratch run
suspected_area: Guess: demo seeding (worker/src/demo.ts) copies the pregame pull as the closing pull and shifts book ts; if production capture does the same it is a real CLV bug
persona: sharp bettor who checks the math
